notes.text: Commonly, aircraft are weighed on scales at 3 locations, either by load cells installed on jacks or roll-on scales at the landing gear. Read each scale for their individual weight; Tricycle gear aircraft will identify these as right-hand and left-hand main landing gear and nose gear (e.g., 1,250 RMLG; 1,200 LMLG; 1,125 NG).
The arm of each weight is its distance from the datum in inches. If a location is in front of the datum, this value will be a negative number (e.g., 120" RMLG; 120" LMLG; -45" NG).
Divide the total moment by the total weight (e.g., 243,375 / 3,575 = 68.07" CG).
The aircraft CG range is found on the TCDS or a given value. If the CG range is 64"-70" on this aircraft, then the CG is within range.
